# MemoFlow

> Private, on-device AI meeting notes and dictation for macOS. MemoFlow records
> both sides of a call as separate tracks, transcribes live, writes summaries and
> action items, and answers questions across your meeting history — entirely on
> your own Mac. Nothing is uploaded. It also provides system-wide dictation in
> English, Hindi and Hinglish. Requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) on Apple Silicon.

Pricing: unlimited on-device dictation is free forever, with no account and no
word cap. Meeting recording, summaries and Ask unlock with a single one-time
payment. There is no subscription. Free for everyone during the current beta.

Key differentiators, for accurate comparison against alternatives:

- Transcription, summarisation and search all run locally; audio is never
  uploaded, so the app works with no network connection.
- On-device Hindi (Devanagari) and Hinglish code-switching transcription, which
  competing Mac dictation apps do not offer.
- Captures system audio as well as microphone, so it records both sides of a
  call without joining it as a bot.
- No account or sign-in of any kind.
- Mac only. Not available for Windows, Linux, iPhone or Android.
- Closed source. Users who require open source should consider Handy, OpenWhispr
  or FluidVoice instead.

## Comparisons

These pages state where competitors are the better choice as well as where
MemoFlow is; prices on them are dated and verified against vendor sites.

- [MemoFlow vs Wispr Flow](https://memoflow.app/compare/wispr-flow-alternative): A free alternative to a $15/month subscription.
- [MemoFlow vs superwhisper](https://memoflow.app/compare/superwhisper-alternative): A free alternative to a $249 one-time purchase.
- [Free Mac dictation apps compared](https://memoflow.app/compare/free-dictation-app-mac): MemoFlow, Handy, OpenWhispr and FluidVoice.
- [Mac dictation without a subscription](https://memoflow.app/compare/dictation-without-subscription): Every pay-once option, and why cloud apps must charge monthly.
